metadata.title: Nothing Left To Remove.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro af_bella) - per-beat mp3 durations are MEASURED, never estimated
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon. SKILL.md limits the HAI persona to the SHORTEST forms only - Hi / Ola / Hej / Ciao. All four are in use, so the lexicon CYCLES least-recently-used first: Hej (03), Ciao (04), Ola (05), Hi (08), Hej (09), Ciao (10). Least recently used is now Ola, last seen at Ep. 05.
metadata.target_runtime: Under 3:00 BY DESIGN. 419 words against Ep. 10's measured 0.3443 s/word predicts 2:24.3, leaving ~35 s of margin. The words-only model is noise of order +-5-10% with NO consistent sign - Ep. 06 +10.4%, Ep. 07 -0.4%, Ep. 08 -5.0%, Ep. 09 +2.7%, Ep. 10 -8.2% - so the margin is for noise in either direction, not for a predicted under-run.
metadata.purpose: Ep. 11 of the AI in Astronomy & Space Science series, from weekly_stem_videos/ideas.md Astronomy topic 11 (AI-designed spacecraft components - generative design for lighter, stronger satellite/rocket parts).
metadata.color_semantics: Claude fidelity palette. Terracotta #D97757 is the ONE accent and marks WHAT THE OPTIMISER DID - the load it was given, the material it kept, the load path it built, and the penalty when that path is cut. Ink marks WHAT A PERSON WOULD HAVE DONE - the solid plate, the uniform material, the dumb baseline that turns out to be the tolerant one. The mapping never flips, so B04 teaches it once and every later plate reads for free. Accented text is #A44A32; #B9B4A0 is strokes and fills only.
metadata.distinct_from_earlier_episodes: Eps. 01-06 had AI inspecting observations; Ep. 07 standing in for a calculation; Ep. 08 a division of labour; Ep. 09 an output that was never a measurement; Ep. 10 a training set produced by the system's own past decisions. Ep. 11 is the first episode where AI produces PHYSICAL HARDWARE, and the first where the model is not wrong at all - the optimum is exactly, provably optimal for the problem as written. The limit is therefore new: not an accuracy ceiling (Ep. 04), an unseen class (Ep. 03), an irreversible rejection (Ep. 05), a latency (Ep. 06), a circularity (Ep. 07), a misreading (Ep. 08), non-identifiability (Ep. 09) or a feedback loop (Ep. 10), but an UNDER-SPECIFIED OBJECTIVE: everything the brief omitted was deleted as surplus, and the deletion is not an error - it is compliance.
metadata.note: ILLUSTRATE LAW: the Claude UI appears at B00, B11, B12, B13. Every other beat illustrates its concept as a reel-local Manim scene (scenes.py). All plates come from assets/gen_struct.py, which runs a real plane-stress finite-element model and a SIMP topology optimiser (assets/topo.py), then a fail-safe damage survey in the published form - a square void swept over the domain, worst case taken (Jansen et al. 2014). THREE claims are ASSERTED and the script writes nothing if any fails; it already refused once, for a threshold I had chosen before measuring. There is NO random number in the pipeline: SIMP from a uniform start is deterministic, so there is no seed to log. PUBLISHED numbers (ESA's 1.4 -> 0.94 kg) and COMPUTED-HERE numbers are kept apart on screen and in the voice. No published figure is reproduced or redrawn. No LaTeX/MathTex anywhere. metadata.channel_title is omitted for the GATE V edge-bleed reason logged in Ep. 03. scenes.py is ASPECT-AWARE: one file lays out 16:9 and the 9:16 derivative, and the two-panel plates ship in both arrangements (shapes/damage side by side, shapes_v/damage_v stacked) because portrait is not a crop.
metadata.reformat: center-cut, focus-aware; pantry/<bid>-916.* is the human replacement slot; -916 overrides honored

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Om Mali. This video is about software that designs spacecraft parts better than people do, and the one thing it quietly throws away while it is doing it.

show.event: the composer types the ask on the cream stage
the send button arms in terracotta
running indicator: solving 7,200 elements
three result lines land in order

props.command: Generative design software is given a volume, some loads and a mass budget, and it returns a part lighter and stiffer than a person would draw. What is it actually optimising, and what does that leave out?
output: it works - same mass, 23% stiffer than a machined plate
the catch - the optimum keeps no spare load path
one small void in the worst place: 31x softer

beats.narration_text: Ten episodes of AI reading the sky. This one is about AI shaping the hardware we send into it.

show.event: OM MALI writes in, terracotta hairline underlines it
role line fades in: Humanitarians AI - presenter
a card draws beside it
row one lands and is STRUCK: ten episodes / AI reads the sky
row two lands boxed: this one / AI makes the part
series line: Ep. 11 - the optimiser deletes the margin

beats.narration_text: You give it a volume, the loads, and a mass budget. It returns a shape no engineer would draw, lighter and stiffer. It gets there by deleting everything that was not carrying your load.

show.event: a card draws on the cream stage
line one types: YOU GIVE IT THREE THINGS, sub: volume, loads, budget
line two: IT GIVES BACK A SHAPE, sub: lighter and stiffer
line three lands in the accent and is UNDERLINED: IT GETS THERE BY DELETING
closer: everything not carrying your load

beats.narration_text: This is not a demo. The bracket holding Sentinel-1's S-band antenna was designed this way. One point four kilos, down to nine hundred and forty grams. A third lighter, on a real satellite.

show.event: an isotype bracket silhouette draws in ink
a published-ledger chip lands: ESA, Sentinel-1
a mass bar runs down from 1.4 kg and STOPS at 0.94 kg
the delta fills terracotta: a third lighter
a small tag: selective laser melting, RUAG with Altair and EOS
closer: it already flies

beats.narration_text: So I built the same problem. A block of metal it may carve, a bolted root, one lug, one load, and a budget. Use forty percent of the metal.

show.event: domain.png fades in: the design volume
the hatched root is ringed
the solid lug is ringed
the terracotta load arrow draws down
a budget chip lands: 40% of the volume
closer: that is the whole brief

beats.narration_text: Then it runs. Material flows toward whatever is carrying load, and starves everywhere else. Nobody drew this. It is the answer to the question I typed.

show.event: evolve.png panel one: uniform grey
panel two lands: structure begins to separate
panel three lands: members thicken, voids open
panel four lands: a finished truss
an iteration counter runs 1 to 90
closer: nobody drew this

beats.narration_text: And it works. Against a plate machined down to the same forty percent, the optimised bracket is twenty-three percent stiffer. Same mass, better shape. That is the pitch, and the pitch is true.

show.event: shapes.png: the thinned plate, then the bracket
two mass chips land, both reading 40%
a stiffness bar pair grows to value
the accent counter lands: 23% stiffer
closer: the pitch is true

beats.narration_text: Now look at where the load travels. Every member is working. There is no second path, because a second path would have been spare mass, and spare mass is what I told it to delete.

show.event: paths.png fades in: strain energy on the bracket
the carrying members light terracotta one after another
a tally lands: every member working
a ghost arrow looks for an alternative route and finds none
the phrase SPARE MASS is struck through
closer: that was the instruction

beats.narration_text: So drill one small void, in the worst place. Less than one percent of the area. The plate gets twenty percent softer. The bracket gets thirty-one times softer. Same void.

show.event: damage.png: the bracket and the plate, same void marked
a chip lands: 0.89% of the area
the plate's bar nudges: 1.2x
the bracket's bar runs away off the scale: 31.2x
the scale relabels itself to contain it
closer: same void, same place

beats.narration_text: And this is known. The fail-safe literature says it plainly. Optimise for one load case and you get a structure with no alternative load paths. Aerospace requires them. Nobody asked the optimiser for them.

show.event: a quotation card draws, published not measured here
the phrase NO ALTERNATIVE LOAD-PATHS types in, accented
a second card: fail-safe design is an aerospace requirement
a third, smaller: and AI-designed hardware already flies - NASA ST5, three evolved antennas, 2006
closer: nobody asked for them

beats.narration_text: So the tell. The margin is buyable. At sixty percent mass the worst void costs sixty percent instead of thirty-one times, and it is still stiffer than the plate. The saving falls from sixty percent to forty.

show.event: price.png draws: compliance against mass budget
the undamaged line is steady and low
the worst-case line plunges as mass is added
a marker lands at 60% mass: 1.6x, not 31x
the saving counter rolls back: 60% to 40%
closer: a third of the saving, given back

beats.narration_text: So: it optimises what you wrote down. Lighter was in the brief. Surviving damage was not. The fix is not a better optimiser. It is a better brief.

show.event: the artefact page opens on the cream stage
line one lands
line two lands
line three lands
line four lands
line five lands in the accent

props.artifactTitle: Nothing Left To Remove - one page
artifactLines: Give it a volume, the loads and a mass budget and it returns a shape no engineer would draw.
It is genuinely better: at the same mass, 23% stiffer than a plate machined to fit.
It got there by deleting everything that was not carrying the load you specified - including the second load path.
One void in the worst place costs the plate 20% and the optimised bracket 31 times.
Ask for damage tolerance and you get it back, for a third of the mass you just saved.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Read it. Here is what I asked my model to optimise. Tell me what I left out of the objective, and what that omission would cost in the real world. Run it on something you have already shipped.

show.event: the composer types the handoff prompt
the send button arms
three grading lines land

props.command: Here is exactly what I asked my model to optimise. Tell me what I left out of the objective, what failure that omission makes invisible, and the cheapest change to the objective that would catch it.
output: grade it: does it name a failure the metric cannot see
grade it: does it price the fix, not just demand it
grade it: would the fix have changed your last decision
